{"id": "0de29482-7878-4a15-8ba5-31154c3d2e19", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "I can calculate this directly using the pricing data the user already gave me, no AWS lookups needed. I'll use 730 hours per month as the standard assumption for EC2 cost calculations.

EC2 comes to $65.70/month, EBS gp3 storage adds $2.70/month. For DynamoDB, I'm checking whether 20 RCU and 20 WCU provisioned capacity falls within the free tier threshold of 18600 unit-hours (25 units sustained over 744 hours) — at 730 hours, 20 RCU and 20 WCU both stay under that 18600 limit, so DynamoDB capacity costs come out to $0.

I'll settle on 730 hrs/month as the standard basis for EC2 calculations, noting the free-tier threshold assumes 744 hrs. EC2 comes to $65.70, EBS to $2.70, and DynamoDB's 14,600 RCU-hrs stays fully under the 18,600 free-tier threshold.

Totaling it up gives roughly $68.40/month, with the caveat that this assumes the free tier hasn't already been consumed elsewhere in the account, and I'm treating OnDemand pricing as the relevant rate since a Reserved term showing $0.00/hr wouldn't apply absent an actual reservation.

All the data needed is already in the message, so I can compute this directly without any tools -- it's a straightforward ad-hoc calculation rather than an investigation requiring root-cause analysis. I'll lay this out as a clear breakdown table.

"}]}
